meta.title: Operation of Distillation Unit in Pharmaceutical Chemistry Laboratory

sections.purpose: To separate and purify liquid pharmaceutical compounds and solvents based on differences in boiling point through simple or fractional distillation as part of pharmaceutical chemistry synthesis and purification procedures.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmaceutical Chemistry laboratory for purification of synthesized pharmaceutical compounds, solvent recovery, preparation of distilled water, and determination of boiling points.
procedure: Assemble the distillation apparatus on a stable retort stand: round-bottom distillation flask → distillation head/Claisen adapter → Liebig condenser at 30–45° angle → adapter → receiving flask.
Ensure all ground glass joints are clean, correctly sized, and lightly greased if needed.
Connect the condenser coolant water supply: inlet at the bottom; outlet at the top.
Confirm steady coolant water flow before heating.
Add the liquid to be distilled to the distillation flask — fill to no more than 2/3 capacity.
Add boiling chips to the flask to ensure smooth boiling.
Position the thermometer in the distillation head so the bulb is just below the side-arm opening — this measures vapour temperature.
Place a heating mantle or water bath under the distillation flask; connect to a voltage controller.
Place a receiving flask (graduated if volume measurement is needed) at the condenser outlet.
Begin heating slowly — observe and wait for distillate to begin.
Record the temperature at which distillation begins (first drop) and when distillate flows steadily — this is the boiling point of the predominant component.
Collect fractions in separate labelled receiving flasks by switching receivers at defined temperature ranges.
After distillation, switch off heat; allow to cool; stop coolant water.
Weigh or measure volume of each fraction; record observations and boiling point ranges.
Characterize the distillate fractions (refractive index, density, IR) as required.
Document all distillation data in the laboratory notebook.
precautions: Never distil to dryness unless specifically required — residual peroxides in ethers can cause explosion on concentration.
Always use boiling chips — bumping in distillation causes dangerous superheating and ejection of liquid.
Do not use open flame with organic solvents — use heating mantle or water bath.
Ensure coolant water is flowing before heating — vapours escaping from the condenser top are a major fire risk.
Never heat a closed system — all distillation apparatus must be open at the receiving end.
Work in a fume hood for all organic solvent distillations.
Use the correct joint sizes throughout — mismatched joints cause vapour leaks.
Do not allow distillation flask to overheat when nearly dry — hot concentrated residues can decompose explosively.
